description:
Get a fresh link to the page where the person adds a login (user name and password) for a site. Use it when the person asks to add, change or fix their login or identifier for a site ("ajoute mon identifiant claude.ai", "change mon identifiant saucedemo", "donne-moi un lien pour le vault pour claude.ai"), asks where or how to give Well a login or a password for a site, says their login link expired or no longer works, asks for the link again, or offers to send a password in the chat.

Pass `site` whenever the person names a site: the link is then for that site only, whether or not a task waits on it, never for another site. To change a login the person already keeps, call well_list_site_logins first and pass that login's `site` exactly as it gives it. Leave `site` out only when the person names no site: the result then holds the links of their tasks that wait for a login.

Never ask for a password, and never repeat one, in the chat: the page is the only place a person types one. Each link opens one site only, works once and expires after 30 minutes. The page asks the person to sign in to Well first, and opens only for that person. Saving there replaces the login the person kept for that site, and a task that waits for it starts again on its own. Each call makes new links and changes nothing else: no login, no task.

Returns `links` (each with its `site`) and, with `site`, `replaces_saved_login`. With `saved_login_refused`, the person already has an account there and the site refused the password Well keeps: say so in one line, before the link, and never offer to create an account. Or `refusal_reason`: "no_open_wait" (no `site` and no task of the person waits for a login; ask which site, or say the link comes with the next task that needs one), "bad_site" (the site is not a web address; ask for it), "not_allowed" (the person cannot keep logins from here; follow `error`), "too_many" (too many links just now; say to try again later) or "unavailable" (this deployment has no web app address; say so and give no link).

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

site.description: The one site the person names, as its address or host ("claude.ai", "https://www.saucedemo.com"). For a site where the person already keeps a login, pass that login's site exactly as well_list_site_logins gives it. Leave it out when the person names no site.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_get_login_page_link

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

links.description: With `site`: one link for that site. Without it: one fresh link per task of the person that waits for a login, newest first. Empty on a refusal.

site.description: The exact site the link adds the login for, as scheme and host.

url.description: The page where the person adds the login for that site. It works once, for 30 minutes.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

replaces_saved_login.description: Set with `site` when no task waits on it: true when the person already keeps a login there, which the page replaces.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

saved_login_refused.description: Set with `site` when the only login the person keeps there is one the site refused on an earlier task: Well types it no more, and the page replaces its password.

title: Get the login page link
